position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: flamenco × hippie folk × Andalusian Arabic-Mediterranean fusion
position_in_era.historical_role: The album most music historians cite as the founding act of nuevo flamenco — released four years before *La leyenda del tiempo* and explicitly cited as influencing both Veneno (1977) and Camarón's *Leyenda* (1979). Producer Ricardo Pachón's first major flamenco-fusion project; introduced instruments like the mellotron to flamenco for the first time.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 1975 on Movieplay/Gong, produced by Ricardo Pachón. First album of Dolores 'Lole' Montoya and Manuel Molina.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Lole's mother was a Romani cantaora; Manuel was a guitarist with hippie/counter-cultural connections. Their pairing softened cante-jondo's pain into something more lyrical — what Lole later called 'something other than singing from pain'.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Seville in the late-Franco era; the album smuggled hippie-Woodstock affect (love, peace, ecology) into flamenco at a politically charged moment.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Flamenco guitar plus acoustic/folk instrumentation; mellotron — the first time the instrument appears in a flamenco album.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Released without promotion; became a long-tail critical and commercial success and a foundational document of nuevo flamenco.
